scope: All exported UDP fields individually reviewed against original archived RFC sources and isolated tests. Own UDP/IP/PHY path and industry neutral, no CANretry/Ethernetrate/MTU/gateway fallback.
IPv4 and IPv6 normal limits, options/extensions, Jumbo versus ordinary wire and pseudoheader length, no Jumbo fragmentation; complete native8-byte header octets compared fields.
Full versus IPv4-omitted versus qualified IPv6 tunnel checksum scope; computed0 toFFFF, no ordinaryIPv6 zero. Full checksum computation/cryptographic integrity needs actual separate proof.
Perpath MTU/fallback and header subtraction, separate datagram/application segmentation, multicast receiver paths/congestion/reliability and whole source-to-function acceptance.
DPLPMTUD own layer/timers/counters/sizes/ack evidence. Only documented checksum/header/probe3/raise600/selectedIPv4base1200 proposals; actual MTU/ports/IP/PHY/clock remain unknown.
765 isolated tests PASS, 148 native andnine shared suites.
source_revisions: RFC768 28August1980 complete UDP header/length/ports/checksum and no guaranteed delivery/duplicate protection.
RFC8085 March2017 sections3/4/5: congestion, message/IP size, reliability, checksum, controlled networks/multicast/ports. Updated DPLPMTUD reference by RFC8899.
RFC2675 August1999 sections2/3/4: IPv6 Jumbo option, no Fragment header, UDP length0 iff datagram>65535, actual length in pseudoheader.
RFC6935 April2013 section2 IPv6 UDP checksums: default nonzero; specifically enabled tunneling exceptions.
RFC6936 April2013 sections4/5/6: assessed zero-checksum tunnel endpoints/address checks/path robustness/encapsulated integrity; not an ordinary application toggle.
RFC8200 July2017 sections4/5/8: IPv6 base40, extensions,1280minimum link, source fragmentation and upper-layer pseudoheader/checksum.
RFC8899 September2020 sections4/5/6.1: DPLPMTUD at one selected layer, acknowledged probes, typed counters/timers and perpath message-size accounting.
